items.title: [Bugs] SMF reports "IP is used" and "UE IP pool exhausted" after gNB CU/DU restart
items.body: ## Bug Description I am performing an 5G SA E2E connectivity test using one(or multiple) CPE and one gNB. I have observed an intermittent issue whenever I stop and restart the gNB CU/DU. Occasionally, when the SMF attempts to assign IP address 10.60.41.41 to the UE, the program log reports that the IP address is already in use. It appears that the previously allocated UE IP is not being released properly, as if the old IP allocation is still being retained. Whenever this happens, the only workaround is to stop free5GC (using Ctrl+C) and run **run.sh** again. After restarting free5GC, the UE can obtain the IP address successfully and registration completes normally. This issue is intermittent and only occurs after restarting the gNB CU/DU and CPE power off/on. ## To Reproduce Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Ensure UE obtained IP address successfully 2. Kill gNB CU/DU 3. Re-run gNB CU/DU 4. Check free5gc log ## Expected Behavior UE successfully obtained IP after gNB CU/DU resumed ## Screenshots - **SCTP shutdown and NGSetup** - **Registration Accept** - **PDU Session Establishment NOT accept** ## Environment **Please, complete the following information:** - free5GC Version: v4.2.3 - OS: 22.04.5 LTS (Jammy Jellyfish) - Kernel version: 6.8.0-124-generic - go version: go1.26.2 linux/amd64 - C compiler version (optional): gcc version 11.4.0 ## Trace Files ### Configuration Files [free5gc-config_202608.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30697603/free5gc-config_202608.zip) ### PCAP File [after_killcudu_pdu_NOK_202608.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30697676/after_killcudu_pdu_NOK_202608.zip) ### Log File [program log_202608.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30697463/program.log_202608.txt) ## System Architecture (Optional) 5G E2E CPE-->gNB-->free5gc(Build and Install free5GC from source code) Test single/multiple UE attach/registration/PDU Test DL/UL throguhput

items.title: [Bugs] NAS Security Mode Control bypass after successful 5G-AKA re-authentication retains old NAS keys
items.body:
## Summary During mobility registration, the AMF completes a new 5G-AKA authentication and derives a new KAMF, then bypasses NAS Security Mode Control and sends Registration Accept using the old NAS keys. This occurs after an unprotected Registration Request or an integrity-protected Registration Request with an invalid MAC, when the UE already has a registered security context. The AMF explicitly logs `UE has a valid security context - skip security mode control procedure` immediately after authentication succeeds. The packet capture contains no Security Mode Command or Security Mode Complete for the second registration. The UE completes registration and subsequently receives Service Accept while continuing to use its old current NAS security context. This is a **NAS Security Mode Control procedure bypass**: the required post-authentication security-mode exchange, confirmation of the replayed UE security capabilities, and activation of the newly derived NAS security context are skipped. ## Affected component and tested environment | Version | AMF revision | Verification | | -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------ | | free5GC v4.2.2 | [02675d9](https://github.com/free5gc/amf/tree/02675d949f207a95379af458c7e80fabe802d728) | Reproduced on the deployed AMF, with NGAP captures and UE/core logs | | free5GC v4.2.1 | [92b7a3f](https://github.com/free5gc/amf/tree/92b7a3f85764b21b5a94204afc2fb1effff5ed15) | The same faulty decision path is present in the pinned source | The runtime uses one AMF and a 3GPP access through an instrumented UERANSIM v3.2.6-based test UE/gNB. The AMF binary and source were not modified for this test; an isolated configuration enabled trace logging. The initial normal registration selects **128-NIA2 and NEA0**. Consequently, the SHT=2 NAS payloads in this capture are readable without decryption; NEA0 is the initial negotiated algorithm, not a downgrade introduced by this test. The test UE has an existing disabled automatic duplicate-ngKSI check. To cover this condition explicitly, the main reproducer sends Authentication Failure cause 71 when the AMF first reuses ngKSI=0, then answers the subsequent Authentication Request with ngKSI=1. The same SMC bypass occurs with and without this additional step. The read-only key observer records current/non-current/pending contexts before each real NAS input; it sends no NAS messages and does not change those contexts. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Configure a test subscriber with working 5G-AKA credentials. Complete a normal initial registration, including Authentication Response, Security Mode Command/Complete, and Registration Complete. Verify that the UE and AMF are Registered with an active NAS security context. 2. Release the RRC/N2 connection so that the UE becomes CM-IDLE, retaining the registered UE context and its current NAS keys in both endpoints. 3. Send a **Mobility Registration Updating** request (`registration type=2`, 5G-GUTI identity) in an NGAP **InitialUEMessage** carrying the UE's 5G-S-TMSI. Use **SHT=1 with one bit flipped in the four-byte NAS MAC**, or **SHT=0 with no NAS integrity protection**. 4. Receive the new Authentication Request. If it reuses the current ngKSI, send Authentication Failure with cause **71, ngKSI already in use**, and receive the replacement Authentication Request. In the main captured example, ngKSI changes from 0 to 1. 5. Return a correct 5G-AKA Authentication Response containing the valid RES*, protected with the existing current NAS context. The AMF and AUSF confirm authentication success. 6. Observe that the next procedure response is **Registration Accept**, with no intervening NAS Security Mode Command/Complete. 7. Send Registration Complete, then Configuration Update Complete. Release the connection again and send a valid Service Request using the UE's retained current context. Observe **Service Accept**. The SHT=1 test hook builds an ordinary integrity-protected request with the current context and flips `pdu.data()[2] ^= 0x01`, the first MAC octet. It preserves the registration fields. SHT=0 encodes a plain copy of the same request. The request is sent after connection release; it is not an SHT=1 message inserted into UplinkNASTransport on an existing NAS connection. The exact executed harness sequence for the invalid-MAC/new-ngKSI case was: ```text registrationRequest authenticationResponse securityModeComplete registrationComplete configurationUpdateComplete registrationRequestGUTI_regtype2 authenticationFailure_71 authenticationResponse registrationComplete configurationUpdateComplete serviceRequest ``` The first five inputs establish the normal Registered state. The SHT override is `STATE_LEARNING_TEST_REG_SHT=1bad` for the second request; use `0` for the plain-request variant. The injected fault is confined to that request. Subsequent authentication and completion messages use the normal current-context protection. ## Actual behavior and evidence There were **15 completed physical queries and 144 NAS inputs**, with cache disabled: three normal controls and three repetitions of each of the four variants below. All 12 second registrations skipped SMC, accepted Registration Complete, and subsequently returned Service Accept. | Second Registration Request | Additional authentication step | Result | | --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | --------------- | | SHT=0 | Correct Authentication Response | SMC bypass, 3/3 | | SHT=1, invalid MAC | Correct Authentication Response | SMC bypass, 3/3 | | SHT=0 | Cause 71, new ngKSI, correct Authentication Response | SMC bypass, 3/3 | | SHT=1, invalid MAC | Cause 71, new ngKSI, correct Authentication Response | SMC bypass, 3/3 | The control executes SMC during initial registration and returns Service Accept in all three repetitions. The five captures contain 336 decoded NAS-PDUs, including repeated downlink transmissions, with no NGAP decoding errors or unhandled SCTP fragments. ### Representative packet trace Source: `raw/bad-mac-newksi/ngap.pcap`, third repetition, 2026-10-21, UTC+08:00. Frame numbers refer to the complete original capture. Times below are shown to milliseconds; `frames.csv` retains the complete timestamps. | Frame | Time | Direction and NGAP carrier | NAS message and relevant fields | | ----- | ---------------- | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | | 173 | 21:33:20
.344 | UE → AMF
InitialUEMessage | Registration Request; SHT=1, type=2, ngKSI=0, 5G-S-TMSI present; AMF confirms MAC failure | | 174 | 21:33:20
.373 | AMF → UE
DownlinkNASTransport | Authentication Request; SHT=2, ngKSI=0 | | 177 | 21:33:21
.027 | UE → AMF
UplinkNASTransport | Authentication Failure; SHT=2, cause=71 | | 178 | 21:33:21
.028 | AMF → UE
DownlinkNASTransport | Authentication Request; SHT=2, ngKSI=1 | | 182 | 21:33:21
.682 | UE → AMF
UplinkNASTransport | Authentication Response; SHT=2 | | 183 | 21:33:21
.698 | AMF → UE
InitialContextSetupRequest | **Registration Accept; SHT=2, no intervening SMC** | | 186 | 21:33:22
.352 | UE → AMF
UplinkNASTransport | Registration Complete; SHT=2 | | 187 | 21:33:22
.352 | AMF → UE
DownlinkNASTransport | Configuration Update Command; SHT=2 | | 190 | 21:33:23
.006 | UE → AMF
UplinkNASTransport | Configuration Update Complete; SHT=2 | | 196 | 21:33:25
.396 | UE → AMF
InitialUEMessage | Service Request; SHT=1, **ngKSI=0**, 5G-S-TMSI present | | 197 | 21:33:25
.398 | AMF → UE
InitialContextSetupRequest | Service Accept; SHT=2 | Frames 175 and 180 repeat the two Authentication Requests; frame 188 repeats Configuration Update Command. The earlier initial registration in the same capture includes Security Mode Command at frames 155/157 and Security Mode Complete at frame 159. The absence of SMC is specific to the second registration. ### Matching core and UE logs The following core messages occur in order in the same captured repetition. Prefixes are shortened here; the excerpt retains original line numbers and timestamps. ```text 21:33:20.345294 NAS MAC verification failed(received: 0xbea69fcf, expected: 0xbfa69fcf) 21:33:21.027945 Authentication Failure Cause: NgKSI Already In Use 21:33:21.686974 5G AKA confirmation succeeded [AUSF] 21:33:21.697588 ue.DerivateKamf() [key redacted] [AMF] 21:33:21.697645 Authentication → SecurityMode 21:33:21.697703 UE has a valid security context - skip security mode control procedure 21:33:21.697714 SecurityMode → ContextSetup 21:33:21.697860 Send Registration Accept 21:33:22.352760 Handle Registration Complete 21:33:22.352934 ContextSetup → Registered 21:33:25.398120 Handle Service Request 21:33:25.398142 Send Service Accept ``` The UE log records the corresponding events: ```text 21:33:20.373 Authentication Request received 21:33:21.028 Authentication Request received 21:33:21.698 Registration accept received 21:33:21.698 Mobility Registration is successful 21:33:22.353 Configuration Update Command received 21:33:25.400 Service Accept received ``` ### Key/context observations The private key journal and AMF trace establish the following in all 12 affected repetitions. Only relationships and lengths are reported here. | Item after the second AKA and Registration Accept | Observation | | ------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | | AMF KAMF | Changed from the initial registration; matches the UE's new non-current KAMF | | AMF KNASint and KNASenc | Retain the old values from the initial registration | | UE current context | Retains the old KAMF and old NAS keys | | UE new non-current context | Contains the new KAMF; KNASint and KNASenc are each length 0 because SMC has not triggered their derivation | | New-ngKSI variants | UE current ngKSI remains 0; new non-current ngKSI is 1; the later Service Request carries ngKSI=0 and is accepted | Thus the new KAMF is derived at both endpoints, but its NAS keys are not activated. The AMF stores the new KAMF while continuing to use old NAS keys. The UE continues with its old current context, which explains why subsequent NAS completion and service signaling still succeeds. Empty UE non-current NAS-key fields mean **not yet derived**, rather than a comparison between two different derived key values. ## Expected behavior and specification requirements [3GPP TS 33.501 V16.14.0, §6.4.6, Step 3, printed page 63](https://www.etsi.org/deliver/etsi_ts/133500_133599/133501/16.14.00_60/ts_133501v161400p.pdf#page=64) states: > If the authentication of the UE is successful, the AMF shall send the NAS Security Mode Command message. For an initial message whose integrity check failed, SMC also requests the complete initial message in Security Mode Complete. Step 4 requires protected completion before the registration response in Step 5. Bypassing SMC omits this required replay and confirmation. The legitimate omission in Step 1 reuses the context protecting a successfully validated initial message; it does not cover this MAC-failure recovery. The EPS/5GS native-context reuse case in §8.2 also concerns reuse, not this single-AMF new-AKA sequence. [TS 24.501 V16.12.0, §4.4.2.6 and §5.4.2.2](https://www.etsi.org/deliver/etsi_ts/124500_124599/124501/16.12.00_60/ts_124501v161200p.pdf#page=50) defines the switch from current to new NAS keys through SMC. Keeping old keys during authentication is expected; accepting this registration after skipping the required exchange is the defect. The EAP/AMF-relocation case in §5.4.1.2.1 is a different procedure. The expected second flow is therefore: ```text Registration Request with invalid MAC / no integrity protection → Authentication Request → valid Authentication Response → Security Mode Command for the new context → Security Mode Complete, including the initial-message replay as required → Registration Accept → Registration Complete ``` ## Source-level cause The same decision path exists in both pinned versions. Links below identify the tested v4.2.2 revision. 1. [HandleRegistrationRequest, handler.go:435–451](https://github.com/free5gc/amf/blob/02675d949f207a95379af458c7e80fabe802d728/internal/gmm/handler.go#L435-L451) clears `SecurityContextAvailable` for initial registration, but retains it for mobility registration. 2. [NAS handler.go:52–62](https://github.com/free5gc/amf/blob/02675d949f207a95379af458c7e80fabe802d728/internal/nas/handler.go#L52-L62) updates `MacFailed` from each decoded message. A later correctly protected Authentication Response resets it to false, despite the initial Registration Request's failed MAC. 3. [HandleAuthenticationResponse, handler.go:2030–2042](https://github.com/free5gc/amf/blob/02675d949f207a95379af458c7e80fabe802d728/internal/gmm/handler.go#L2030-L2042) sets the new KSEAF, calls `DerivateKamf()`, and sends Authentication Success. [DerivateKamf, amf_ue.go:494–499](https://github.com/free5gc/amf/blob/02675d949f207a95379af458c7e80fabe802d728/internal/context/amf_ue.go#L494-L499) overwrites `ue.Kamf`. 4. [SecurityContextIsValid, amf_ue.go:467–469](https://github.com/free5gc/amf/blob/02675d949f207a95379af458c7e80fabe802d728/internal/context/amf_ue.go#L467-L469) checks only availability, KSI≠7, and `!MacFailed`. It does not distinguish an unchanged current context from a newly derived KAMF awaiting activation. 5. [SecurityMode, sm.go:271–300](https://github.com/free5gc/amf/blob/02675d949f207a95379af458c7e80fabe802d728/internal/gmm/sm.go#L271-L300) treats that predicate as sufficient to emit SecurityMode Success immediately. NAS-key derivation and sending SMC are both in the other branch. This skips both the procedure and `DerivateAlgKey()`, leaving the old NAS keys in place. The corresponding v4.2.1 decision is [sm.go:271–300 at 92b7a3f](https://github.com/free5gc/amf/blob/92b7a3f85764b21b5a94204afc2fb1effff5ed15/internal/gmm/sm.go#L271-L300). ## Security impact and demonstrated scope The AMF marks SecurityMode as successful without exchanging Security Mode Command/Complete after the successful new AKA. This bypasses the required NAS security-mode exchange and its capability/initial-message confirmation, prevents activation of fresh NAS keys, and lets registration and subsequent NAS service signaling proceed using the previous keys. The AMF's stored KAMF and active NAS keys consequently belong to different authentication generations. The reproducer uses a registered subscriber, its existing NAS context, and valid RES* for the new AKA. Identity authentication succeeds. The demonstrated bypass concerns **NAS Security Mode Control and fresh-context activation**. The affected runs maintain NAS service signaling; their measured outcome is old-key retention, not an observed service outage. [free5gc-nas-smc-bypass-evidence.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33773171/free5gc-nas-smc-bypass-evidence.zip)

items.title: [Bugs] SMF Resource Exhaustion via PFCP Session Establishment Failure Handling
items.body:
## Bug Description

A resource exhaustion issue exists in Free5GC v4.2.3 during PFCP Session Establishment failure handling.

During PDU Session establishment, Free5GC uses PFCP signaling over the N4 interface for SMF-UPF communication. If PFCP Session Establishment Responses from the UPF are not received, the SMF continuously retransmits PFCP Session Establishment Requests. However, the resources allocated during the failed session establishment procedure are not properly released.

As a result, repeated failed session establishment attempts can gradually consume UE IP address pool resources. Once the available IP address resources are exhausted, new UEs may fail to establish PDU sessions, causing a denial-of-service (DoS) condition.

## To Reproduce

Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Deploy Free5GC v4.2.3 with a Docker-based 5G Core Network environment.
2. Register multiple UEs and establish normal PDU sessions using UERANSIM.
` docker exec ueransim /ueransim/nr-ue -c /ueransim/config/uecfg.yaml -n 5`
3. Deploy N4Replay between the SMF and UPF as a PFCP interceptor.
    Repository:   https://github.com/hackeryounow/n4repaly/
4. Enable PFCP message interception and drop PFCP Session Establishment Response messages from the UPF.
5. Start a new UE to trigger another PDU Session Establishment procedure.    
`docker exec ueransim /ueransim/nr-ue -c /ueransim/config/uecfg.yaml`
6. Observe that the SMF continuously retransmits PFCP Session Establishment Requests after the responses are dropped.
7. Repeat the procedure multiple times until the available UE IP address pool is exhausted.
8. The continuous PFCP retransmission behavior and resource exhaustion process are shown in the attached animation.

## Expected Behavior

When PFCP Session Establishment fails after retransmission timeout or retry exhaustion, Free5GC should properly release all temporarily allocated resources associated with the failed session establishment procedure.
The SMF should terminate the failed procedure and allow subsequent UEs to establish PDU sessions normally.

## Screenshots

A demonstration video is provided: [https://youtu.be/E1e14Nr_3OA](https://youtu.be/E1e14Nr_3OA)

## Environment

**Please complete the following information:**

- free5GC Version: v4.2.3
- Deployment: Docker-based 5G Core Network
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04 Desktop
- Kernel version: 138~22.04.1-Ubuntu
- go version: 1.21.8 linux/amd64

## Trace Files

- Configuration Files:
The Free5GC configuration files are provided under `n4repaly/5gc/free5gc/` in the attached archive.
The UE IP address pool network prefix was modified to `/29` to facilitate reproduction of the resource exhaustion behavior.
- PCAP File:
  `multi-est-pfcp-session-free5gc.pcapng` contains the PFCP signaling traces between SMF and UPF.
- Log File:
  `smf.log` contains the SMF log output during the reproduction.


## System Architecture (Optional)
The test environment consists of: 
- 5G Core Network: Free5GC v4.2.3
- UE simulator: UERANSIM
- PFCP test component: [N4Replay](https://github.com/hackeryounow/n4repaly)
- Interface under test: N4 interface between SMF and UPF
Architecture:
```
UERANSIM
   |
   |
Free5GC AMF/SMF -------- N4Replay -------- UPF
                              |
                              |
                    PFCP message interception
                    and response dropping
```
Deployment environment:
- Containerized deployment using Docker
- SMF and UPF communicate through PFCP over the N4 interface
## Additional Context

- Vulnerability Type:  Resource Exhaustion（Denial of Service）
- CVSS v4：`CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:H/AT:P/PR:L/UI:N/VC:L/VI:H/VA:H/SC:L/SI:L/SA:H`

items.title: [Bugs] NSSF lacks object-level authorization on NSSAI availability updates and subscriptions
items.body:
[Originally posted as advisory GHSA-5cv4-2x7f-6g8h]

**Related:** [#849](https://github.com/free5gc/free5gc/issues/849) already reports `PUT`/`DELETE` on an arbitrary `{nfId}` and deletion of another NF's subscription. Open PR [free5gc/nssf#54](https://github.com/free5gc/nssf/pull/54) restricts the `nnssf-nssaiavailability` token to the AMF NF type but adds no per-object check, so one AMF can still act on another AMF's entry. 

This issue additionally demonstrates creation of entries for unknown `nfId` values and its effect on slice selection, and the subscription-ID allocator issuing duplicate IDs.

## Description

Two defects in the NSSF permit an NF holding an `nnssf-nssaiavailability` token to act on
resources belonging to other NFs, which is a textbook BOLA vulnerability.

**Affected endpoints:**

Part 1 — all three methods on `/nnssf-nssaiavailability/v1/nssai-availability/{nfId}` take the
target AMF from the path and never compare it against the caller:

- `PUT` — overwrites the victim AMF's supported-S-NSSAI list, and creates an entry if none exists
- `PATCH` — the same exposure, applied as a patch document
- `DELETE` — removes the victim AMF's entry from `AmfList` outright, matching on `nfId` alone

Part 2 — `DELETE /nnssf-nssaiavailability/v1/nssai-availability/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}`

(`PATCH .../subscriptions/{subscriptionId}` is a 501 stub at `api_nssaiavailability.go:197-199`
and is not affected.)

**Affected files:**

- `internal/sbi/api_nssaiavailability.go` (lines 154–195, dispatch at 194)
- `internal/sbi/processor/nssaiavailability_store.go` (lines 58–78 for `DELETE`, 203–243 for `PUT`)
- `internal/sbi/processor/nssaiavailability_subscription.go` (lines 27–56, 92–105)

**Affected versions:** free5GC v4.3.0 ships exactly the reviewed NSSF commit (`c1092f6`); current
NSSF `main` is still affected.

### Root Cause Analysis

**Part 1 — `nfId` is an unchecked selector, and also a creator.**

```go
// internal/sbi/api_nssaiavailability.go:154-194
func (s *Server) NSSAIAvailabilityPut(c *gin.Context) {
    var params NssaiAvailabilityPutParams
    if err := c.ShouldBindUri(&params); err != nil { ... 400 ... }
    ...
    s.Processor().NssaiAvailabilityNfInstanceUpdate(c, nssaiAvailabilityInfo, params.NfId)
}
```

The only validation on the way in is URI binding (a UUID-formatted `nfId`), JSON deserialization and
a check that the listed S-NSSAIs are supported in the PLMN — none of which concerns the caller. The processor then
locates the AMF configuration by that ID and — if none is configured — **creates** one:

```go
// internal/sbi/processor/nssaiavailability_store.go:219-236
// Find AMF configuration of given NfId
for ... {
    if amfConfig.NfId == nfId { ... }
}
...
amfConfig.NfId = nfId
```

So `nfId` is not merely an unchecked selector over existing objects; it also permits creation of
configuration under arbitrary (UUID-formatted) identifiers.

`NSSAIAvailabilityDelete` and `NSSAIAvailabilityPatch` reach the same table by the same key.
`NssaiAvailabilityNfInstanceDelete` needs no request body at all:

```go
// internal/sbi/processor/nssaiavailability_store.go:60-69
for i, amfConfig := range factory.NssfConfig.Configuration.AmfList {
    if amfConfig.NfId == nfId {
        factory.NssfConfig.Configuration.AmfList = append(
            factory.NssfConfig.Configuration.AmfList[:i],
            factory.NssfConfig.Configuration.AmfList[i+1:]...)
        c.Status(http.StatusNoContent)
        return
    }
}
```

Across the module, every comparison of `nfId` against another identifier has the form
`amfConfig.NfId == nfId` — a lookup keyed on the path parameter. There is no comparison against a
caller identity anywhere in the NSSF, and no claim identifying the caller is ever read.

Note that, this is not something a correct token validation can fix. Token validation authenticates the caller; it cannot establish *which objects* that caller may address, because the scope `nnssf-nssaiavailability` is service-level and
every AMF in the network legitimately holds one. We confirmed this by execution: running the real
`NssaiAvailabilityNfInstanceDelete` handler behind a fully hardened validator, an expired token, a
wrong-audience token and a wrong-issuer token are each rejected with 401 and the victim's entry
survives, while a token satisfying all three checks and issued to a different AMF erases the
victim AMF's availability entry with 204.

**Part 2 — predictable ID reuse plus unauthorized unsubscribe.**

```go
// nssaiavailability_subscription.go:31-53
var idx uint32 = 1
for _, sub := range factory.NssfConfig.Subscriptions {
    tempID, err := strconv.Atoi(sub.SubscriptionId)
    if err != nil { return subscription, err }
    if uint32(tempID) == idx {
        if idx == math.MaxUint32 { ... }
        idx++
    } else {
        break        // (annotation) assumes sorted: first gap ends the scan
    }
}

subscription.SubscriptionId = strconv.Itoa(int(idx))
...
factory.NssfConfig.Subscriptions = append(factory.NssfConfig.Subscriptions, subscription)
```

The gap scan assumes the slice is sorted ascending, but the new entry is always **appended** rather
than inserted in sorted position. Reusing a freed ID therefore breaks the invariant: from `[1, 3]`,
issuing ID 2 gives `[1, 3, 2]`. The next scan walks 1 → 2, meets `3 ≠ 2`, breaks early, and
re-issues **2** — already in use: `[1, 3, 2, 2]`.

```go
// nssaiavailability_subscription.go:92-105
func (p *Processor) NssaiAvailabilitySubscriptionUnsubscribe(c *gin.Context, subscriptionId string) {
    ...
    for i, subscription := range factory.NssfConfig.Subscriptions {
        if subscription.SubscriptionId == subscriptionId {
            factory.NssfConfig.Subscriptions = append(factory.NssfConfig.Subscriptions[:i],
                factory.NssfConfig.Subscriptions[i+1:]...)
            c.Status(http.StatusNoContent)
            return
        }
    }
```

Unsubscribe matches on the subscription ID alone; the caller's identity is never consulted (also
reported in [#849](https://github.com/free5gc/free5gc/issues/849)).

### PoC

Part 1's `DELETE` path was confirmed by execution against the commit reviewed, driving the real
`NssaiAvailabilityNfInstanceDelete` handler behind an authorization check.

**Part 1 — overwrite a victim AMF's slice availability:**

1. Obtain any access token whose scope includes `nnssf-nssaiavailability`
2. Identify a victim AMF's NF Instance ID — these are UUIDs exchanged over the SBI and visible in
   NRF discovery responses
3. `PUT /nnssf-nssaiavailability/v1/nssai-availability/{victim-amf-uuid}` with an
   `NssaiAvailabilityInfo` body declaring an empty supported-S-NSSAI list, or any list of PLMN-supported S-NSSAIs
4. `NSSAIAvailabilityPut` binds `params.NfId` and dispatches at `:194` with no identity comparison;
   the processor updates the victim's entry at `:222-230`, or creates one at `:234-243` when the
   `nfId` is unknown
5. `DELETE` on the same URI is a shorter route to the same effect — no body is required, and
   `NssaiAvailabilityNfInstanceDelete` removes the victim's entry and returns 204

**Part 2 — blind erasure of a victim's subscription:**

1. Attacker subscribes, receives ID 1, then unsubscribes, freeing it
2. Victim NF (e.g. an AMF) subscribes and is assigned the reused ID 1
3. Attacker sends `DELETE .../subscriptions/1`; the loop at `:97` matches on ID alone and deletes
   the victim's subscription with 204

### Impact

NSSAI availability drives slice selection, and the table the attacker writes is the one the
selection logic reads. `AmfList[].SupportedNssaiAvailabilityData` is consumed by
`CheckSupportedSnssaiInAmfTa` (`internal/util/util.go:198-214`), which gates the AMF re-selection
branch at `nsselection_network_slice_information.go:588`, and by `AddAmfInformation`
(`internal/util/util.go:510-534`) when it builds `CandidateAmfList`.

An attacker who writes an empty or narrow list for a victim AMF therefore makes
`CheckAllowedNssaiInAmfTa` return false for that AMF on registration-time NS-selection requests
that carry a TAI: the NSSF declares it unable to serve the UE and returns candidate AMFs instead,
steering registrations away from the victim AMF. An over-broad list produces the converse — the
NSSF affirms the AMF for slices it does not support. `DELETE` reaches the first outcome in one
request with no body.

Because writes are accepted for unknown `nfId` values, an attacker can also insert entries under
identifiers of their own choosing, and `AddAmfInformation` appends `amfConfig.NfId` to
`CandidateAmfList` (`util.go:531`) — so an attacker-chosen NF Instance ID can be handed back to the
network as a candidate AMF. This last path is conditional: `AmfSetList` is evaluated first and
returns early (`util.go:471-505`), and free5GC's shipped `nssfcfg.yaml` does define an `amfSetList`
carrying availability data, so the `AmfList` loop is reached only when no configured AMF Set can
serve the UE.

Part 2 lets any caller remove another NF's availability subscription silently. free5GC's NSSF does
not currently send NSSAI availability notifications, so the immediate effect is on subscription
state: duplicate IDs corrupt the subscription table, so a later unsubscribe may remove an entry
other than the one intended.

### Suggested fix

1. Require the authenticated caller's NF Instance ID (from the token's `sub` claim) to equal the
   `nfId` path parameter, rejecting with 403 otherwise
2. Allow `PUT` to create an entry only for the caller's own `nfId` (TS 29.531 uses `PUT` to
   "replace or create" the NF's own NSSAI availability information), rather than silently creating
   configuration for arbitrary identifiers
3. Replace the gap scan with a monotonically increasing counter or a UUID — reusing identifiers for
   security-relevant resources is best avoided entirely. If reuse is retained, insert in sorted
   position so the scan's invariant holds
4. Record the creating NF's identity on each subscription and require it to match the caller in
   `NssaiAvailabilitySubscriptionUnsubscribe`

### References

- OWASP API Security Top 10 — API1:2023 Broken Object Level Authorization

items.title: [Bugs] UDM: subscriptionId accepted without validation, leaks internal error on oversized/crafted input (GHSA-f72w-jgfw-hhm9)
items.body:
## Bug Description
`HandleUnsubscribeForSharedData`, `HandleModifyForSharedData`, and `HandleUnsubscribe` in `internal/sbi/api_subscriberdatamanagement.go` extract `subscriptionId` from the path and pass it straight to the processor with no format/length validation — unlike `supi`/`ueId` in the same file, validated via `validator.IsValidSupi()`/`IsValidGpsi()`. Oversized or special-character values propagate deep enough to trigger an unhandled internal error that leaks implementation details.

Full technical writeup, PoC and CVSS scoring: GHSA-f72w-jgfw-hhm9
https://github.com/free5gc/free5gc/security/advisories/GHSA-f72w-jgfw-hhm9

Status: accepted by maintainers, CVE requested (not yet assigned).

## To Reproduce
```shell
curl -v -X DELETE "http://<UDM_IP>:80/nudm-sdm/v2/shared-data-subscriptions/$(python3 -c 'print("A"*10000)')"
# 500, {"detail":"unsupported scheme[]", "cause":"SYSTEM_FAILURE"}

curl -v -X DELETE 'http://<UDM_IP>:80/nudm-sdm/v2/shared-data-subscriptions/%24ne'
# 500, same detail

curl -v -X PATCH "http://<UDM_IP>:80/nudm-sdm/v2/shared-data-subscriptions/%7B%22%24ne%22%3Anull%7D" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{}'
# 404, {"title":"User not found","cause":"USER_NOT_FOUND"} — reaches business logic instead of being rejected at input validation
```

## Expected Behavior
`subscriptionId` should be validated (e.g. UUID or the format used at generation time) immediately after extraction, returning 400 with a generic message on failure — mirroring the existing `supi`/`ueId` pattern.

## Environment
- free5GC Version: v4.2.3

## Walkthrough
Add a validation check for `subscriptionId` before calling the processor, following the pattern already used for `supi`/`ueId` in `HandleGetAmData`/`HandleUnsubscribe`. Avoid propagating `err.Error()` verbatim to the client.

## Additional Context
The `500 "unsupported scheme[]"` suggests the value is later passed to something expecting a well-formed URI (e.g. `url.Parse`) without the caller anticipating arbitrary input at that stage.

items.title: [Bugs] UPF silently returns Cause=Accepted when RemoveBAR fails — gtp5g kernel buffer never released on session teardown, enabling memory exhaustion DoS; compounded by BAR-ID length field not validated allowing ID spoofing
items.body: ## Bug Decription A SessionModificationRequest containing a RemoveBAR IE referencing a non-existent BAR-ID causes the UPF to log a goroutine stack trace but unconditionally return Cause=RequestAccepted. The BAR removal silently fails. The gtp5g kernel-space packet buffer associated with the BAR is never released. This is exploitable as a kernel memory exhaustion DoS: during PDU session release or paging state transitions, the SMF sends RemoveBAR to release the kernel buffer allocated for IDLE-state packet buffering. If the PFCP-layer BAR state diverges from gtp5g's kernel state (via a prior double-remove or attacker-induced desync), RemoveBAR fails silently — the kernel buffer is never reclaimed. An attacker with N4 access can trigger this per-session with a single crafted packet, permanently leaking one kernel buffer slot per targeted session. In a production core handling thousands of simultaneous IDLE-state UEs, sustained triggering exhausts kernel memory allocated to gtp5g, causing OOM conditions in the kernel module and a complete data-plane buffering DoS affecting all UEs attempting paging state transitions. A second independently reportable vulnerability is exposed in the same trigger path: BAR-ID IE length is not validated. Per 3GPP TS 29.244 §8.2.118, BAR-ID is a fixed 1-octet field. The UPF silently accepts a 4-byte BAR-ID IE encoding, discards the upper 3 bytes, and uses the truncated value as the lookup key — with no error, no cause code, and no log warning. This allows an attacker to reference BAR-ID=0x00000001 (4-byte encoding, truncated to BAR(0x0)) to target a completely different BAR than declared, bypassing any application-layer control that keys on the nominal BAR-ID value. Impact Kernel memory exhaustion DoS via unreleased gtp5g buffers: Each silently failed RemoveBAR permanently retains a kernel-space packet buffer. Under sustained attack targeting IDLE-state sessions, gtp5g's buffer pool is exhausted, rendering paging state transitions (IDLE→CONNECTED handover data delivery) impossible for all UEs — a full data-plane availability DoS. Indefinite packet retention: Packets buffered for released sessions remain in kernel memory indefinitely, occupying buffer slots that can never be flushed and never be delivered. System restart is the only recovery. BAR-ID spoofing via length field abuse: A RemoveBAR IE with BAR-ID declared as 4 bytes but encoding a value with a non-zero upper byte targets a different BAR than the nominal ID suggests. An attacker can craft BAR-ID=0x00000100 (nominal=256, truncated=0) to remove BAR(0) while the message appears to reference the non-existent BAR(256) — bypassing any session-level access control that filters on declared BAR-ID. Compound vulnerability with RemoveFAR / session teardown: During session release, SMF typically sends RemovePDR + RemoveFAR + RemoveBAR in sequence. Silent failure of RemoveBAR combined with the RemoveFAR silent failure (above) means both the forwarding rule and the buffer are permanently retained — the released session is effectively immortal in the kernel. Internal path disclosure: Full goroutine stack trace on every trigger. Root Cause NFs/upf/internal/pfcp/session.go, handleSessionModificationRequest, line 239: err = sess.RemoveBAR(i) if err != nil { sess.log.Errorf("Mod RemoveBAR error: %+v", err) // error discarded — kernel buffer never released; Cause=RequestAccepted returned } NFs/upf/internal/pfcp/node.go, (*Sess).RemoveBAR, line 483: func (s *Sess) RemoveBAR(id uint8) error { if _, ok := s.BARs[id]; !ok { return fmt.Errorf("RemoveBAR: BAR(%#x) not found", id) } // ... } Secondary — BAR-ID IE length not validated (IE parsing layer): A BAR-ID IE with length=4 is accepted without error; only the least-significant byte is extracted as the uint8 key. No Cause=MandatoryIEIncorrect or length-mismatch rejection is issued, violating 3GPP TS 29.244 §7.6. ## To Reproduce Steps to reproduce the behavior: Run: python3 free5gc_upf_remove_bar_not_found_repro.py [free5gc_upf_remove_bar_not_found_repro.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26703895/free5gc_upf_remove_bar_not_found_repro.py) ## Expected Behavior When RemoveBAR fails, the UPF must return Cause=RuleCreationModificationFailure per 3GPP TS 29.244 §7.5.4. Silent acceptance of a failed BAR removal leaves an unreleased kernel buffer — a directly exploitable memory exhaustion DoS vector. A BAR-ID IE with declared length ≠ 1 byte must be rejected with Cause=MandatoryIEIncorrect per 3GPP TS 29.244 §7.6. Silently truncating an oversized BAR-ID enables ID spoofing attacks against the BAR lookup table. ## Screenshots ## Environment free5GC Version: v4.2.1] OS: Ubuntu 22.04 Kernel version: normal go version: normal C compiler version (optional): normal ## Trace Files ### Configuration Files version: 1.0.3 description: UPF initial local configuration pfcp: addr: 127.0.0.8 # IP addr for listening nodeID: 127.0.0.8 # External IP or FQDN can be reached retransTimeout: 1s # retransmission timeout maxRetrans: 3 # the max number of retransmission ### PCAP File [free5gc_upf_remove_bar_not_found_repro.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26703888/free5gc_upf_remove_bar_not_found_repro.zip) ### Log File 2026-04-14T08:02:11.790920556Z [INFO][UPF][PFCP][LAddr:127.0.0.8:8805] handleSessionModificationRequest 2026-04-14T08:02:11.790960780Z [ERRO][UPF][PFCP][LAddr:127.0.0.8:8805][CPNodeID:127.0.0.100][CPSEID:0x7005][UPSEID:0x1] Mod RemoveBAR error: RemoveBAR: BAR(0x0) not found github.com/free5gc/go-upf/internal/pfcp.(*Sess).RemoveBAR /home/fei/free5gc/NFs/upf/internal/pfcp/node.go:483 github.com/free5gc/go-upf/internal/pfcp.(*PfcpServer).handleSessionModificationRequest /home/fei/free5gc/NFs/upf/internal/pfcp/session.go:239 github.com/free5gc/go-upf/internal/pfcp.(*PfcpServer).reqDispacher /home/fei/free5gc/NFs/upf/internal/pfcp/dispacher.go:23 github.com/free5gc/go-upf/internal/pfcp.(*PfcpServer).main /home/fei/free5gc/NFs/upf/internal/pfcp/pfcp.go:156 runtime.goexit /home/fei/go/pkg/mod/golang.org/toolchain@v0.0.1-go1.25.5.linux-amd64/src/runtime/asm_amd64.s:1693

items.title: [Bugs] SMF panics with unrecovered type assertion when PCF returns SMPolicyControl.CreateSMPolicyError instead of ProblemDetails during PDU Session Establishment
items.body: ## Bug Decription While handling PDU Session Establishment, SMF calls PCF's `Npcf_SMPolicyControl_CreateSMPolicy` service. When that call fails, `NFs/smf/internal/sbi/processor/pdu_session.go:194` performs an **unchecked, single-value type assertion**: ```go problemDetails := openapiError.Model().(models.ProblemDetails) ``` This assumes PCF's error body always deserializes to the generic `models.ProblemDetails` type. However, per 3GPP TS 29.512, `CreateSMPolicy` can also return the more specific `SMPolicyControl.CreateSMPolicyError` type — for example, when PCF cannot find the target subscriber's SM Policy Data in UDR. When PCF returns that specific type, the assertion panics. The panic is caught by gin's recover middleware, so the SMF process itself does not crash, but the PDU Session Establishment request fails with HTTP 500 and a full stack trace is printed to the log every time this path is hit — a functional denial of service for any subscriber whose SM Policy Data lookup fails this way, plus log/CPU noise from repeated triggering. Notably, PCF's own consumer code for the exact same kind of response (`NFs/pcf/internal/sbi/consumer/udr_service.go`, `amf_service.go`) consistently uses the safe two-value form (`problemDetails, ok := ...Model().(models.ProblemDetails); if ok { ... }`) everywhere. The unsafe single-value form at `pdu_session.go:194` appears to be an isolated oversight rather than an intentional design choice — grepping the whole SMF source tree, this is the only call site using the unsafe form. ## To Reproduce Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Change config: none required. This reproduces on a completely default free5GC deployment — no subscriber needs to be provisioned in the subscriber database, no NF config needs to be modified. 2. Code patch: none, default `main` branch code reproduces this. 3. Run command: start free5GC normally (all NFs registered via NRF as usual), then send a single crafted `POST /nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts` request directly to SMF — no real UE, gNB, or NGAP registration flow is needed. The request body is a `multipart/related` `SmContextCreateData` with any `supi` that has no SM Policy Data in the subscriber database (any SUPI not provisioned at all trivially satisfies this). See attached `repro.sh` (pure `curl`, no other dependency) — it can be run standalone against any SMF instance, only the `servingNfId`/`guami`/`smContextStatusUri` placeholder values may need adjusting if your deployment validates them more strictly than a stock config does. 4. Dump packet: attached, see `free5gc_smf_crash_repro.pcap` (loopback capture of exactly the reproduction request/response in step 3, `host 127.0.0.2 and port 8000`, HTTP/2 cleartext so payloads are visible in Wireshark). [repro.sh](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30165279/repro.sh) ## Expected Behavior SMF should handle the `SMPolicyControl.CreateSMPolicyError` response type gracefully (e.g. using the same safe type-assertion pattern already used elsewhere in the codebase) and return an appropriate 4xx error to its own caller (AMF), instead of panicking and returning an uncontrolled 500 with a stack trace. ## Screenshots ## Environment - free5GC Version: v4.2.1 (commit `69ba98ff8eba69a8092c56abb80a01fcd483e7b3`, 2026-03-20) - OS: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS Server - Kernel version: 6.8.0-124-generic - go version: go1.25.5 linux/amd64 - C compiler version (optional): not applicable, no cgo components involved in this path ## Trace Files ### Configuration Files [config.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30165385/config.zip) ### PCAP File [free5gc_smf_crash_repro.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30165387/free5gc_smf_crash_repro.zip) ### Log File [smf_panic.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30165390/smf_panic.log)

items.title: [Bugs] SMF PCFSelection panics on empty NRF discovery result during PDU session establishment
items.body:
## Bug Decription
`SMF`, when establishing a new PDU session, calls `PCFSelection` to discover a PCF via NRF (`/nnrf-disc/v1/nf-instances?target-nf-type=PCF&...`). The consumer-side handler in `internal/sbi/consumer/nrf_service.go:441-442` indexes the NRF discovery response **without checking whether `NfInstances` is empty**. When NRF returns a successful `200 OK` whose body has `"nfInstances": null` (or `[]`, or the field absent), `res.SearchResult.NfInstances[0]` panics with `runtime error: index out of range [0] with length 0`.

The defect is glaring because the **sister function `CHFSelection` five lines above guards the access correctly**:

```go
// internal/sbi/consumer/nrf_service.go (deployed v4.2.2 — SMF v1.4.3 line numbers,
//                                       identical at upstream master commit 2232d29)

// CHFSelection — properly guarded
func (s *nnrfService) CHFSelection(smContext *smf_context.SMContext) error {
    ...
    res, err := client.NFInstancesStoreApi.SearchNFInstances(ctx, request)
    if err != nil {
        logger.ConsumerLog.Errorf("SearchNFInstances failed: %+v", err)
        return err
    }
    if res != nil && len(res.SearchResult.NfInstances) > 0 {        // ← guard
        smContext.SelectedCHFProfile = res.SearchResult.NfInstances[0]
        return nil
    }
    return fmt.Errorf("no CHF found in CHFSelection")
}

// PCFSelection — UNGUARDED  (lines 416-444)
func (s *nnrfService) PCFSelection(smContext *smf_context.SMContext) error {
    ...
    res, err := client.NFInstancesStoreApi.SearchNFInstances(ctx, request)
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }
    // Select PCF from available PCF
    smContext.SelectedPCFProfile = res.SearchResult.NfInstances[0]   // ← line 442: panic
    return nil
}
```

`SearchResult.NfInstances` is typed `[]NrfNfDiscoveryNfProfile,omitempty`. When NRF has no matching PCF instance — either because no PCF is registered, NRF discovery filters exclude all candidates, or an attacker controls the NRF response (NRF NFM PUT is unauthenticated, see free5gc/free5gc#990) — NRF returns a syntactically-valid `200 OK` whose body looks like:

```json
{"validityPeriod":100,"nfInstances":null}
```

`json.Unmarshal` happily fills `NfInstances` with a zero-length slice (or nil-slice for `null`). The unguarded `[0]` access panics deterministically.

`PCFSelection` is invoked on **every** new PDU session establishment via this chain (`internal/sbi/processor/pdu_session.go:212`):

```go
// BSF-aware PCF selection: first check BSF for existing PCF binding
if bsfErr := p.Consumer().BSFAwarePCFSelection(smContext); bsfErr != nil {
    smContext.Log.Errorln("PCF selection error (with BSF integration):", bsfErr)
    // Fallback to traditional PCF selection if BSF integration fails
    if fallbackErr := p.Consumer().PCFSelection(smContext); fallbackErr != nil {
        smContext.Log.Errorln("fallback PCF selection error:", fallbackErr)
    }
}
```

`BSFAwarePCFSelection` (`internal/sbi/consumer/bsf_service.go:152-198`) tries BSF first, falls back to `PCFSelection` for any new session — and itself contains a similar but **properly guarded** access at line 188 (`if searchErr != nil || res == nil || len(res.SearchResult.NfInstances) == 0`). So BSFAwarePCFSelection's own NRF query is safe; the panic site is the explicit fallback at line 442.



## To Reproduce
The panic requires SMF to invoke `PCFSelection` **and** for NRF to return zero PCF instances. Two equally-realistic triggers cover this:

### Reproducer A — PCF unregistered / unhealthy

Realistic operational failure mode: PCF crashed, scaled to zero, or is in the process of registering when a UE attempts a fresh PDU session.

#### Step 1 — remove PCF from NRF

```bash
docker stop pcf
docker exec <mongo-container> mongo free5gc --quiet --eval \
  'db.NfProfile.deleteMany({nfType:"PCF"})'

# Verify NRF discovery returns empty:
SMF_INST=$(docker exec <mongo-container> mongo free5gc --quiet --eval \
  'db.NfProfile.findOne({nfType:"SMF"},{nfInstanceId:1,_id:0}).nfInstanceId' | tail -1 | tr -d '"')
DISC_TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST 'http://10.100.200.4:8000/oauth2/token' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  --data-urlencode 'grant_type=client_credentials' \
  --data-urlencode 'nfType=SMF' \
  --data-urlencode "nfInstanceId=$SMF_INST" \
  --data-urlencode 'targetNfType=NRF' \
  --data-urlencode 'scope=nnrf-disc' \
  | python3 -c 'import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["access_token"])')

curl -s "http://10.100.200.4:8000/nnrf-disc/v1/nf-instances?target-nf-type=PCF&requester-nf-type=SMF" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DISC_TOKEN"
# → {"validityPeriod":100,"nfInstances":null}      ← drives the bug
```

#### Step 2 — trigger a fresh PDU session via UERANSIM

```bash
# nr-gnb pointing at AMF SCTP, nr-ue with fresh SUPI
./nr-gnb -c gnb.yaml &
./nr-ue  -c ue.yaml &
# UE registers, requests PDU session for DNN=internet
# → AMF forwards N1 PduSessionEstablishmentRequest → SMF HTTPPostSmContexts
# → SMF calls BSFAwarePCFSelection → fallback PCFSelection → PANIC
```

#### Step 3 — observe the panic in `docker logs smf`

```text
[INFO][SMF][PduSess]  Receive Create SM Context Request
[INFO][SMF][Consumer] No PCF binding found in BSF, using NRF discovery for SUPI: imsi-208930000000099, DNN: internet
[ERRO][SMF][GIN] panic: runtime error: index out of range [0] with length 0
goroutine NNN [running]:
panic({0x...?, 0x...?})
        /usr/local/go/src/runtime/panic.go:783 +0x132
github.com/free5gc/smf/internal/sbi/consumer.(*nnrfService).PCFSelection(0x..., 0x...)
        /go/src/free5gc/NFs/smf/internal/sbi/consumer/nrf_service.go:442 +0x...
github.com/free5gc/smf/internal/sbi/consumer.(*nbsfService).PCFSelectionWithBSF(0x..., 0x...)
        /go/src/free5gc/NFs/smf/internal/sbi/consumer/bsf_service.go:195 +0x...
github.com/free5gc/smf/internal/sbi/consumer.(*Consumer).BSFAwarePCFSelection(0x..., 0x...)
        /go/src/free5gc/NFs/smf/internal/sbi/consumer/consumer.go:74 +0x...
github.com/free5gc/smf/internal/sbi/processor.(*Processor).HandlePduSessionContextReplacement(0x..., 0x..., 0x...)
        /go/src/free5gc/NFs/smf/internal/sbi/processor/pdu_session.go:212 +0x...
github.com/free5gc/smf/internal/sbi.(*Server).HTTPPostSmContexts(0x..., 0x...)
        /go/src/free5gc/NFs/smf/internal/sbi/api_pdusession.go:103 +0x...
```

The PDU session establishment fails. SMF stays up because Gin's `defer recover()` catches the panic, but every subsequent attempt while PCF is missing reproduces the same panic. Each panic also leaves a half-allocated `SMContext` in the SMF pool, which compounds over time.

### Reproducer B — attacker-controlled NRF discovery filter

NRF NFM PUT is **unauthenticated** (free5gc/free5gc#990). An attacker can (a) deregister legitimate PCF profiles by `DELETE /nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances/<id>`, (b) register one bogus PCF that doesn't match the SMF's discovery filter, or (c) modify NRF mongo directly to inject a `nf-discovery` blacklist. Any of these turn NRF discovery into an "empty result" response, with no need to take down the real PCF.

```bash
# (a) — silent: deregister legitimate PCFs (NFM endpoint, no token)
for id in $(curl -s 'http://10.100.200.4:8000/nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances?nf-type=PCF' \
              | python3 -c 'import sys,json; [print(p["nfInstanceId"]) for p in json.load(sys.stdin)["NFProfiles"]]'); do
  curl -s -X DELETE "http://10.100.200.4:8000/nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances/$id"
done
# any subsequent UE PDU session → SMF panic
```

### Direct deterministic proof (independent of the lab)

Reproducible in 30 lines of Go without any free5gc deployment:

```go
package main

import (
    "encoding/json"
    "fmt"

    "github.com/free5gc/openapi/nrf/NFDiscovery"
)

func main() {
    for _, body := range []string{
        `{"validityPeriod":100,"nfInstances":null}`,
        `{"validityPeriod":100,"nfInstances":[]}`,
        `{"validityPeriod":100}`,
    } {
        var resp NFDiscovery.SearchNFInstancesResponse
        _ = json.Unmarshal([]byte(body), &resp.SearchResult)
        defer func() { recover() }()
        // Mirror smf/internal/sbi/consumer/nrf_service.go:442
        _ = resp.SearchResult.NfInstances[0]
    }
}
```

Output (validated on `github.com/free5gc/openapi@v1.2.3`):

```text
body="{\"validityPeriod\":100,\"nfInstances\":null}"  NfInstances len=0  nil?=true
    >>> PANIC at NfInstances[0]: runtime error: index out of range [0] with length 0 <<<
body="{\"validityPeriod\":100,\"nfInstances\":[]}"    NfInstances len=0  nil?=false
    >>> PANIC at NfInstances[0]: runtime error: index out of range [0] with length 0 <<<
body="{\"validityPeriod\":100}"                       NfInstances len=0  nil?=true
    >>> PANIC at NfInstances[0]: runtime error: index out of range [0] with length 0 <<<
```

All three NRF response shapes — the lab-observed `"nfInstances":null`, the explicit empty array, and the absent field — deterministically trigger the panic at the `[0]` access.

## Expected Behavior
Apply the **same length guard already used by the sister `CHFSelection` function five lines above** in the same file:

```go
// PCFSelection — fixed
func (s *nnrfService) PCFSelection(smContext *smf_context.SMContext) error {
    ...
    res, err := client.NFInstancesStoreApi.SearchNFInstances(ctx, request)
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }
    if res == nil || len(res.SearchResult.NfInstances) == 0 {
        return fmt.Errorf("no PCF found in PCFSelection")
    }
    smContext.SelectedPCFProfile = res.SearchResult.NfInstances[0]
    return nil
}
```

When PCFSelection legitimately fails (no PCF available), SMF should reject the PDU session establishment with `5GSM cause #38 Network Failure` (or `#27 Missing or unknown DNN` per TS 24.501) — never crash the goroutine. The caller at `pdu_session.go:215` already has a fallback path; it expects an `error` return, not a panic.

The same scan should be repeated across other free5gc consumer trees for the `<slice>[0]` shape; this defect class is symmetric with the AMF `*Pointer` consumer-deref family and is just as exploitable.

## Environment
- free5GC Version: `v4.2.2`
- SMF binary: `free5gc/smf:v4.2.2` (commit `2232d299`, build time `2026-04-21T03:13:45Z`). The same `nrf_service.go:441-442` lines are **unfixed at the latest upstream master commit `2232d29`** (no `len() > 0` guard added). Validated by `git log -1` + manual diff against `/tmp/smf_latest`.

- Kernel version: `6.14.0-37-generic`
- go version: `go1.25.5 linux/amd64` (build toolchain; runtime: `free5gc/smf:v4.2.2` Docker image)
- Validation date: `2026-04-30`
- Deployment: Docker-based lab on the internal SBI network `10.100.200.0/24`. SMF `10.100.200.13`, NRF `10.100.200.4`, PCF `10.100.200.3`, AMF `10.100.200.16`, MongoDB container `081af9111608_mongodb`.

items.title: [Bugs] Installation of NFs via `go install` no longer works
items.body:
## Describe the bug
Installation of most of NFs via `go install` command no longer works because tag `v1.3.0` has already been used in past with a different commit number, and cached by proxy.golang.org.

Even if the official installation method works (cloning git repo and running make), having `go install` not working this is unexpected and misleading because `go install` is the usual and recommended way of installing go programs according to https://go.dev/ref/mod#go-install.

## To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. `go install github.com/free5gc/amf/cmd@v1.2.7` is working as expected
2. `go install github.com/free5gc/amf/cmd@v1.3.0`
```
go: github.com/free5gc/amf/cmd@v1.3.0: module github.com/free5gc/amf@v1.3.0 found, but does not contain package github.com/free5gc/amf/cmd
```
3. `go install github.com/free5gc/amf@v1.3.0 &&  ~/.local/share/go/bin/amf -h` is showing outdated options names
```
2025-03-03T16:15:46+01:00 [INFO][AMF][App] amf
2025-03-03T16:15:46+01:00 [INFO][AMF][App] AMF version:  
        Not specify ldflags (which link version) during go build
        go version: go1.23.5 linux/amd64
NAME:
   amf - -free5gccfg common configuration file -amfcfg amf configuration file

USAGE:
   amf [global options] command [command options] [arguments...]

COMMANDS:
   help, h  Shows a list of commands or help for one command

GLOBAL OPTIONS:
   --free5gccfg value  common config file
   --amfcfg value      amf config file
   --help, -h          show help
```
4. `curl https://proxy.golang.org/github.com/free5gc/smf/@v/v1.3.0.info` shows this is a version from 2021
```
{"Version":"v1.3.0","Time":"2021-01-18T15:45:43Z"}
```

## Expected behavior
I expected the actual `v1.3.0` from 2025 of NFs to be installed, not an old version from 2021.

## Workaround
1. Publish a `v1.3.1` for the following NFs:
  - amf
  - ausf
  - n3iwf
  - nrf
  - nssf
  - pcf
  - udm
  - udr
  - smf
2. Stop reusing previously used tags.

## Environment
 - free5GC Version: 4.0.0
 - OS: debian 12
 - Kernel version:  6.1.128-1 (2025-02-07)
 - go version:  go1.23.5 linux/amd64
 - c compiler version (Option): not relevant

## Additional Context
I use `go install` syntax to build Docker images of some NFs:
```dockerfile
RUN ${COMMIT:? Missing build-arg COMMIT.} && go install \
     -ldflags="-X github.com/free5gc/util/version.VERSION=https://github.com/louisroyer-docker/free5gc -X github.com/free5gc/util/version.BUILD_TIME= -X github.com/free5gc/util/version.COMMIT_HASH=${COMMIT} -X github.com/free5gc/util/version.COMMIT_TIME=" \
     github.com/free5gc/amf/cmd@${COMMIT}

#…

COPY --from=builder /go/bin/cmd /usr/local/bin/amf
```
